subject: Hosting pathway statement and decision asks — private/VPC & compliance
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medisect.health>, Tom Baker <tom.baker@procureware.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Oct 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting pathway statement and decision asks — private/VPC & compliance

Elena / Tom — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick synthesis of the things we heard and the concrete asks to keep momentum. Please correct anything I’ve misstated.

Key pain points and drivers
- Data residency: patient records and analytics must remain in the EU (GDPR + national healthcare guidance).
- Regulatory air‑gap preference for critical ML workloads (Medisect is evaluating an air‑gapped inference tier for model hosting).
- Procurement window: procurement will need a commercial SOW and security evidence by mid‑Nov to land budget for H1.29.
- Ops friction: limited outbound egress, strict IP whitelists, and mature change control are non‑negotiable.

Goals we heard
- Proof of concept hosted in customer VPC (EU region) with isolated subnet and strict NAT/firewall rules.
- Ability to run nightly batch inference in an air‑gapped mode for PHI data.
- KMS/HSM integration for key material; customer-managed keys preferred.

Technical constraints (from the call)
- No public internet egress from inference hosts except to specific telemetry endpoints.
- Max sustained throughput target for first phase: ~3k tokens/s (burstable); expect steady 500 tokens/s.
- Firewall whitelist only; IPs will be provided during procurement.

Asks / next steps (owner and ETA)
1) We (Redwood) to produce a short "hosting pathway statement" that maps three deployment options (Hosted VPC, Dedicated-in-VPC, On‑prem appliance) to the compliance/ops constraints above. (Owner: Karthik) — deliver by 2028‑10‑07. [Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-onepager.pdf]
2) Medisect to confirm the internal stakeholders to approve procurement (Legal, Procurement, Infosec), and preferred timeline window. (Owner: Elena) — reply by 2028‑10‑09.
3) Marcus to share a network runbook template that lists required ports, probing rules, and sample firewall ACLs. (Owner: Marcus) — deliver by 2028‑10‑06. [Attachment: network-runbook-template.xlsx]
4) Tom / Procurement to share any mandatory contract clauses or procurement milestones so we can align SOW language. (Owner: Tom) — reply by 2028‑10‑11.

If that matches, can we lock a 30‑minute follow up the week of Oct 9 to review the hosting pathway statement and map to Medisect's procurement deadlines?

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.com]
[Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-onepager.pdf]

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medisect.health>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@procureware.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Oct 2028 18:04:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Hosting pathway statement and decision asks — private/VPC & compliance

Karthik — thanks for pulling this together, that aligns well. A couple of clarifications and notes from our side:

Corrections / clarifications
- Timeline: procurement is targeting a vendor shortlist by the week of Nov 13, so we need SOW + security evidence before then (earlier is better).
- Compliance: in addition to GDPR, we need a DPA with EU SCCs and a copy of any SOC/ISO attestation.
- Air‑gap: we do not require a fully air‑gapped physical environment for phase 1. We need an isolated VPC with the ability to sever outbound egress on demand for escalation scenarios.

Stakeholders
- Legal: Marta Cruz (marta.cruz@medisect.health) — she'll own contract redlines.
- InfoSec: Lukas Meier (lukas.meier@medisect.health) — technical security signoff.
- Procurement: Tom is already looped.

Accepts the asks. Marcus — if you can share a minimal runbook (ports + sample egress block) that will help Lukas validate compatibility with our network team.

I'll confirm a 30‑minute slot for Oct 10 or 11 once I hear back from Marta.

Best,
Elena
Director of Platform Security, Medisect Health
[Attachment: procurement-timeline.pdf]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medisect.health>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting pathway statement and decision asks — private/VPC & compliance

Elena / team — attaching the network runbook template and a short HSM/KMS note. A couple of technical clarifications inline below and a small ask for a bandwidth profile.

Inline notes
- We can support per‑customer VPC deployments where Redwood components run in customer‑managed subnets (no public IPs on inference nodes).
- Telemetry/metrics: we can route minimal telemetry to an endpoint you own; for fully blocked scenarios we provide delayed batch telemetry uploads from a controlled bastion.
- Private key handling: we'll support a bring‑your‑own‑KMS flow; HSM integration requires an initial configuration window and an HSM cert exchange. See short notes attached. [Attachment: hsm-integration-notes.txt]

Ask for bandwidth profiling
- To size burst capacity and to propose batching settings we need: typical request size (tokens/request), expected concurrent users hitting the inference API during peak, and any scheduled nightly bulk runs (volume and start time). If you can send a short table we’ll match to our throughput profiles.

I’ve attached: network-runbook-template.xlsx and hsm-integration-notes.txt.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network-runbook-template.xlsx]

- Redwood (Karthik) to provide the hosting pathway one‑pager by Oct 7.

Regards,
Tom
